claim_verdicts.evidence: Re-extracted this round: `git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:DonHang.Infrastructure/LoggingNotifier.cs` lines 9-13 match the lesson's block character-for-character, including `public void Send(int orderId, string subject) => logger.LogInformation("notification for order {OrderId}: {Subject}", orderId, subject);`. One message template, two named placeholders ({OrderId}, {Subject}), two arguments after the template.

Re-extracted this round: `git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Middleware/RequestLoggingMiddleware.cs` lines 9-24 match the lesson's block character-for-character, including `logger.LogInformation("{Method} {Path} responded {StatusCode} in {ElapsedMs}ms", context.Request.Method, context.Request.Path, context.Response.StatusCode, stopwatch.ElapsedMilliseconds);`. Four placeholders, four arguments, same order.

Logging overview, "Log message template": "Each log API uses a message template. The message template can contain placeholders for which arguments are provided. Use names for the placeholders, not numbers. The order of placeholders, not their names, determines which parameters are used to provide their values." and "The arguments themselves are passed to the logging system, not just the formatted message template. This enables logging providers to store the parameter values as fields." The first also settles the lesson's "matched to its placeholder by position, not by name".

Re-run live 2026-09-25 against the running lab: login, then POST /api/v1/orders returned 201; `docker logs donhang-api --since 40s` printed as plain text "info: DonHang.Infrastructure.LoggingNotifier[0]" then the indented "notification for order 27: order placed". The container runs with ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development and no console-formatter override (docker-compose.yml api service, DonHang.Api/appsettings.json), so this is the default simple console formatter.
claim_verdicts.source: live: docker logs donhang-api --since 40s; examples/don-hang @ stage-1 docker-compose.yml (api), DonHang.Api/appsettings.json

claim_verdicts.evidence: C# reference, "Compilation of interpolated strings": "If an interpolated string has the type `string`, the compiler typically transforms it into a String.Format method call." and "The compiler checks if an interpolated string is assigned to a type that satisfies the interpolated string handler pattern." `LogInformation(string? message, params object?[] args)` takes `string`, not a handler type, so the value is finished before the call - exactly the condition the claim now carries.

`git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs`: PlaceOrderAsync ends with `await repository.AddAsync(order); await repository.SaveChangesAsync(); notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed"); return order;` (line 21), with no condition around the Send. Confirmed live: one POST /api/v1/orders produced exactly one "notification for order 27: order placed" line. A second call site, notifier.Send(order.Id, "order cancelled") at line 36, belongs to CancelOrderAsync and is not what the lesson cites.

issues.text: False of this system, and it is the payoff sentence of the section. A 500 here can only come from ExceptionHandlingMiddleware catch-all, registered OUTSIDE RequestLoggingMiddleware (Program.cs). When a request throws, the exception unwinds past `await next(context)` and the LogInformation carrying {StatusCode} never runs. Verified live: a POST that threw ArgumentException gave a 400, an ExceptionHandlingMiddleware warning, and no RequestLoggingMiddleware line at all. So StatusCode=500 matches nothing in this app, and 4xx failures are not 500 either.
issues.fix: Replace the example with one this code supports, e.g.: "filtering `Path=/api/v1/orders` finds every order request that reached the end of the pipeline, whatever order it was for". Keep the condition section 4 established ("for a tool built to read the event's fields") on both filtering examples, including `OrderId=41`, which is stated here as if the app could do it today.
issues.quote: filtering `StatusCode=500` finds every request that failed, regardless of which order it was for

issues.text: The gloss is unconditional where the platform is not: a logging call produces a record only when the level is enabled for its category - this repo's own appsettings.json sets "Microsoft.AspNetCore": "Warning", so Information calls in that category produce nothing - and .NET 10 documents sampling and buffering, which can drop a record too. Separately, the .NET docs name this record a "log record"/"log entry"; "log event" appears there only in "Log event ID" (the EventId), a different thing the reader meets later.
issues.fix: Change the bullet to: "log event - the record a logging call produces when that level is enabled for it. Its fields exist on this record regardless of how any particular tool later prints it (the .NET documentation calls this record a log record)."
issues.quote: log event - the one record a single logging call produces.
